items.english: However, thinking it over afterwards, this was still the part that was less painful. — Before long his throat grows parched. Liu too knows the story of how Cao Mengde, or someone, cured the thirst of his soldiers by telling them there was a plum grove ahead. But now, picture as he will the sweet sourness of plums in his mind, his thirst is not a whit the less for it. He moves his jaw about, he bites his tongue, yet inside his mouth still keeps its heat. That too might still have been somewhat easier to bear, had there not been the unglazed earthen jar at his pillow. From the mouth of the jar the heavy smell of wine comes without break to assail his nose. And, though it may be fancy, he even feels that smell growing stronger with every minute. Thinking at least to look at the jar, Liu opened his eyes. Glancing upward, he sees the mouth of the jar and something like half of its amply bulging body. That alone is what he sees, but at the same time there rises before Liu's imagination the sight of wine the colour of gold brimming in the dim interior of that jar. Before he knew it he had licked his cracked lips with his dry tongue, yet there is no sign at all of saliva springing. Even the sweat, dried now by the sun, no longer flows as before.
